Disappearance.description:
The morning Aris was found gone, made once at world creation: who distrusted her bionics,
and the facts around it. Nobody in the village made her vanish.

distrusted_by.description: The residents who distrusted her bionics, each once, never Aris. They're evasive about her, and some lie.
distrusted_by.title: Distrusted By

facts.description: Who distrusted her, who saw her last and what the clues hold. Each has its own id, and their leads go to one another. Their knowers grow as residents pass them on.
facts.title: Facts

Disappearance.title: Disappearance

Fact.description:
Something that happened, or how someone felt, kept in the sim. Residents only voice it:
code decides who tells it to whom, and who lies about it.

what.description: What happened or how someone felt, in the third person, as it really was. Each knower's memory of it is in their own words.
what.title: What

where.description: A location's id, such as "maker_space", or a map's, such as "high_street".
where.title: Where

about.description: Who it's about, even if those who know it couldn't name them.
about.title: About

known_by.description: The residents who know it, each listed once: the only record of who does. Whoever passes it on adds a `told` knower with `learned_by`.
known_by.title: Known By

found_in.description: The clue the player can find it in instead of being told, such as Aris's notes: the interactable's id. Null if only residents can tell it.
found_in.title: Found In

leads.description: Where learning it points the player next, never back to itself. Hearing a lie about it opens none.
leads.title: Leads

Fact.title: Fact

HowKnown.description:
How a resident knows a fact. `did`: it's what they did or felt. `witnessed`: they saw or
heard it. `told`: someone told them.
HowKnown.title: HowKnown

JournalEntry.description: Something the player learned about Aris's disappearance: a fact, or a lie told about one.

fact_id.description: The fact it's about. Several entries can be about one fact.
fact_id.title: Fact Id

text.description: What they learned, as the journal puts it. A lie is written as it was told.
text.title: Text

source.description: Who told them, or the clue they found it in.

flushed.description: Whether the infrared eye saw the resident flush as they told it, which it shows exactly on a lie. Null if the player had no infrared eye then, and for a clue.
flushed.title: Flushed

leads.description: The leads it opened that are still open: its fact's leads, and none for a lie. Each closes once any entry is about its fact, a lie included.
leads.title: Leads

JournalEntry.title: JournalEntry

Knower.description:
A resident who knows a fact, how they know it, and how willing they are to tell it.
Whoever passes a fact on, by telling or gossip, sets the new knower's `tells_from` and
`cover`.

tells_from.description: The least trust they need in whoever asks before they tell it: 0 tells anyone. Null if they never tell it.
tells_from.title: Tells From

cover.description: What they say instead of telling it, when they lie, e.g. "Aris and I always got on fine." Code decides when they lie, as for other lies, so the infrared eye reads it exactly. Null if they keep quiet rather than lie.
cover.title: Cover

Knower.title: Knower

Lead.description:
Where the trail goes next: someone to ask or somewhere to look, which turns up a fact. It
closes once the journal has any entry about that fact, a lie included.

fact_id.description: The fact following it turns up.
fact_id.title: Fact Id

text.description: For the journal, e.g. "Kofi saw her the evening before she went missing. Ask him where she was going."
text.title: Text

Lead.title: Lead

Source.description: Who told the player something, or the clue they found it in.

id.description: The resident's id, or the clue's interactable's.
id.title: Id

name.description: As the journal names them, e.g. "Kofi" or "Aris's notes".
name.title: Name

Source.title: Source

SourceKind.description:
Where the player learned something: a `resident` told them, or they found a `clue`, such
as Aris's notes or a terminal.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

description:
The story and the player's journal of it, saved with the world. One object holds both, so
it can be restored in place before the world has made its story.

disappearance.description: Null until the world makes it, as in a save from before it.

journal.description: What the player has learned, in the order they learned it.
journal.title: Journal

title: Investigation
